blocks.source: El Indulto Cuento, texto completo. Emilia Pardo Bazán, de cuantas mujeres enjabonaban ropa en el lavadero público de Marineda, aterridas por el frío cruel de una mañana de marzo. Antonia, la asistenta, era la más encorvada, la más abatida, la que torcía con menos frío, la que refregaba con mayor desaliento. A veces, interrumpiendo su labor, pasabas el dorso de la mano.
blocks.translation: The Indulto Cuento, complete text. Emilia Pardo Bazán, one of the women who washed clothes in the public laundry of Marineda, terrified by the cruel cold of a March morning. Antonia, the maid, was the most stooped, the most disheartened, the one who twisted the clothes with the least resistance, the one who rubbed them with the most despair. Sometimes, while she was working, you would pass your hand over the back of hers.

blocks.source: Por los enrojecidos párpados y las gotas de agua y las burbujas de jabón parecían lágrimas sobre su tés marchita. Las compañeras de trabajo de Antonia la miraban compasivamente. Y de tiempo en tiempo, entre la algarabía de las conversaciones y disputas, se cruzaba un breve diálogo a media voz, entretejido con exclamaciones de asombro, indignación y lástima. Todo el lavadero sabía al dedillo los males de la asistenta y hallaba en ellos asunto para interminables comentarios.
blocks.translation: The reddened eyelids, the tears and the soap bubbles seemed to be mirroring Antonia's distress over her tea. Her colleagues watched her with compassion. And from time to time, amidst the noise of conversations and arguments, a brief, hushed dialogue would occur, filled with expressions of astonishment, outrage, and pity. Everyone in the laundry knew Antonia's problems intimately and found endless material for comment.

blocks.source: Nadie ignoraba que la infeliz, casada con un mozo carnicero, residía años antes, en compañía de su madre y de su marido en un barrio extramuros, y que la familia vivía con desahogo, gracias al ácido trabajo de Antonia y a los cuartejos ahorrados por la vieja en su antiguo oficio de revendedora, baratillera y prestamista. Nadie había olvidado tampoco la lúgubre tarde en que la vieja fue asesinada, encontrándose hecha astillas la tapa del arcón donde guardaba sus caudales y ciertos pendientes y brincos de oro. Nadie, tampoco. El horror que infundió en el público la nueva de que el ladrón y asesino no era sino el marido de Antonia, según esta misma declaraba, añadiendo que desde tiempo atrás roía al criminal la codicia del dinero de su suegra, con el cual deseaba establecer una tablajería suya propia.
blocks.translation: No one was unaware that the unhappy woman, who was married to a butcher, had previously lived with her mother and husband in a neighborhood outside the city walls, and that the family was living comfortably, thanks to Antonia's hard work and the savings accumulated by the old woman in her previous profession as a reseller, a bottle seller, and a moneylender. No one had also forgotten the gloomy afternoon when the old woman was murdered, with the lid of the chest where she kept her valuables and certain gold earrings and necklaces broken. No one had. The horror that the news of the thief and murderer, who was actually Antonia's husband, caused in the public, added to the fact that Antonia had long been secretly coveting her mother-in-law's money, with which she intended to establish her own carpentry business.

blocks.source: Sin embargo, el acusado hizo por probar la coartada, valiéndose del testimonio de dos o tres amigotes de taberna. Y de tal modo, envolvió el asunto que, en vez de ir al palo, salió con 20 años de cadena, no fue tan indulgente la opinión como la ley. Además de la declaración de la esposa, había un invicio vehementísimo. La cuchillada que mató a la vieja.
blocks.translation: However, the defendant attempted to prove his alibi, relying on the testimony of two or three acquaintances from the tavern. As a result, the case was handled in a way that, instead of leading to a conviction, resulted in a sentence of 20 years in prison. The legal system was not as lenient as the situation warranted. In addition to the wife's testimony, there was also a very strong motive. The stabbing that killed the old woman.

blocks.source: Cuchillada certera y limpia, asestada, de arriba abajo, como las que los matachines dan a los cerdos, con un cuchillo ancho y afiladísimo de cortar carne. Para el pueblo no cabía duda en que el culpable debió subir al cadalzo y el destino de Antonia comenzó a infundir sagrado terror cuando fue esparciéndose el rumor de que su marido se la había jurado para el día en que saliese del presidio por acusarle. La desdichada quedaba en cinta y el asesino la dejó avisada de que a su vuelta se contase entre los difuntos. Cuando nació el hijo de Antonia, esta no pudo criarlo, tal era su debilidad y demacración y la frecuencia de las congojas que desde el crimen la aquejaban.
blocks.translation: A precise and clean stabbing, performed from above downwards, similar to how matachines attack pigs with a sharp, meat-cutting knife. For the villagers, it was clear that the culprit must have climbed onto the well and Antonia's fate began to instill a sense of sacred terror when the rumor spread that her husband had vowed to kill her upon his release from prison, after she had been accused. The unfortunate woman was left in suspense, and the killer warned her that upon his return, she would be counted among the dead. When Antonia's son was born, she was unable to care for him, due to her weakness and frailty, and the constant suffering that plagued her since the crime.

blocks.source: Y como no le permitía el estado de su bolsillo pagarama, las mujeres del barrio que tenían niños de pecho dieron de mamar por turno a la criatura que creció en clenque, resintiéndose de todas las angustias de su madre. Un tanto repuesta ya, Antonia se aplicó con ardor al trabajo. Y aunque siempre tenían sus mejillas, esa azulada palidez que se observa en los enfermos del recobró su silenciosa actividad, su aire apacible. Veinte años de cadena.
blocks.translation: And, as the state wouldn't allow him to pay for childcare, the women in the neighborhood who had young children would take turns feeding the child, who grew up in the orphanage, experiencing all the anxieties of his mother. Antonia, who was now somewhat recovered, dedicated herself with great determination to her work. And although she always had a pale complexion, the bluish hue that is often seen in patients returned to her calm and peaceful demeanor. Twenty years in prison.

blocks.source: En veinte años pensaba ella para sus adentros. Él se puede morir o me puedo morir yo. Y de aquí allá falta mucho todavía. La hipótesis de la muerte natural no la asustaba, pero la espantaba imaginar solamente que volvía su marido.
blocks.translation: Over the past twenty years, she had thought about these things deeply. He could die, or I could die. And there was still a long way to go. The idea of his natural death didn't frighten her, but the thought of him returning was terrifying.

blocks.source: En vano las cariñosas vecinas la consolaban indicándole la esperanza remota de que el inico parricida se arrepintiese, se enmendase o, como decían ellas, se volviese de mejor idea. Meneaba Antonia la cabeza entonces murmurando sombríamente. ¿Eso él? ¿De mejor idea?
blocks.translation: The kind neighbors tried to comfort her, suggesting that the only perpetrator might regret his actions, change his ways, or, as they put it, "come to his senses." Antonia shook her head, muttering darkly. "Could he? Could he really change?"

blocks.source: ¿Cómo no baje Dios del cielo en persona y le saque aquel corazón perro y le ponga otro? Y al hablar del criminal, un escalofrío corría por el cuerpo de Antonia. En fin, veinte años tienen muchos días y el tiempo aplaca la pena más cruel. Algunas veces figurábasele a Antonia que todo lo ocurrido era un sueño o que la ancha boca del presidio que se había tragado al culpable no le devolvería jamás.
blocks.translation: How could God have descended from heaven and removed that heart, replacing it with another? And when Antonia thought about the criminal, a chill ran down her spine. In any case, twenty years is a long time, and time can soften even the most cruel punishment. Sometimes Antonia imagined that everything that had happened was a dream, or that the wide-mouthed prison that had swallowed up the guilty man would never release him.

blocks.source: O que aquella ley que al cabo supo castigar el primer crimen sabría prevenir el segundo, la ley. Esa entidad moral de la cual se formaba Antonia un concepto misterioso y confuso. Era sin duda fuerza terrible, pero protectora. Mano de hierro que la sostendría al borde del abismo.
blocks.translation: Or, that law, which eventually proved capable of punishing the first crime, would also prevent the second. That moral force, of which Antonia had a mysterious and confusing concept, was undoubtedly a terrible, but also protective, power. It was a strong hand that would keep her from falling into the abyss.

blocks.source: Así es que a sus ilimitados temores se unía una confianza indefinible, fundada sobre todo en el tiempo transcurrido y en el que aún faltaba para cumplirse la condena. Singular enlace el de los acontecimientos. No creería de seguro el rey cuando vestido de capitán general y con el pecho cargado de condecoraciones daba la mano ante el ara a una princesa que aquel acto solemne costaba amarguras sin cuenta a una pobre asistenta en lejana capital de provincia. Así que Antonia supo que había recaído indulto en su esposo.
blocks.translation: Therefore, his unlimited fears were compounded by an indefinable confidence, based primarily on the time that had passed and the time remaining before the sentence was carried out. A particularly striking example was the king's act. Dressed as a general and with numerous decorations on his chest, he extended his hand to a princess, an act that, according to the poor assistant in a distant provincial capital, would have caused immense bitterness. Antonia, therefore, knew that her husband had been granted a pardon.

blocks.source: No pronunció palabra y la vieron las vecinas sentada en el de la puerta con las manos cruzadas, la cabeza caída sobre el pecho, mientras el niño, alzando su cara triste de criatura enfermiza, jimoteaba. Mi madre, cálienteme la sopa. Por Dios, que tengo hambre. El coro benévolo y cacareador de las vecinas rodeó a Antonia.
blocks.translation: She didn't say a word, and the neighbors saw her sitting by the door, her arms crossed, her head resting on her chest, while the child, with his sickly, mournful expression, whimpered. "Mom, please, can you warm up the soup? I'm so hungry." The chorus of sympathetic and concerned neighbors surrounded Antonia.

blocks.source: Algunas se dedicaron a arreglar la comida del niño. Otras animaban a la madre del mejor modo que sabían. Era bien tonta en afligirse así. Ave María Purísima.
blocks.translation: Some were focused on preparing the child's meal. Others tried to comfort the mother in the best way they could. It was quite absurd for her to be so upset. Holy Mary, Mother of God.

blocks.source: No parece sino que aquel hombrón no tenía más que llegar y matarla. Había gobierno, gracias a Dios y audiencia y serenos. Se podía acudir a los celadores, al alcalde. ¿Qué alcalde?
blocks.translation: It seemed like all he wanted was to arrive and kill her. There was a government, thanks to God, and a court, and a calm atmosphere. You could go to the guards, to the mayor. But which mayor?

blocks.source: Decía ella con osca mirada y apagado acento. ¿O al gobernador? ¿O al regente? ¿O al jefe de municipales?
blocks.translation: "She said this with a piercing gaze and a subdued accent. Or was it the governor? Or the regent? Or the head of the municipal department?"

blocks.source: Había que ir a un abogado. Saber lo que dispone la ley, una buena moza, casada con un guardia civil, ofreció enviar a su marido para que le metiese un miedo al picarón. Otra, resuelta y morena, se brindó a quedarse todas las noches a dormir en casa de la asistenta. En suma, tales y tantas fueron las muestras de interés de la vecindad que Antonia se resolvió a intentar algo.
blocks.translation: We needed to consult a lawyer. Knowing what the law allowed, a young woman, married to a police officer, offered to send her husband to intimidate the troublemaker. Another, determined and dark-haired, offered to stay overnight at the caretaker's house. In short, these were just a few examples of the neighborhood's concern, which motivated Antonia to take action.

blocks.source: Y sin levantar la sesión, acordó se consultar a un jurisperito a ver qué recetaba. Cuando Antonia volvió de la consulta, más pálida que de costumbre, de cada tenducho y de cada cuarto, bajos salían mujeres en pelo a preguntarle noticias y se oían exclamaciones de horror. La ley, en vez de protegerla, obligaba a la hija de la víctima a vivir bajo el mismo techo maritalmente con el asesino. ¿Qué ley es divino señor de los cielos?
blocks.translation: And without interrupting the session, they agreed to consult with a legal expert to determine the appropriate course of action. When Antonia returned from the consultation, looking even paler than usual, women with dark hair were emerging from every room and hallway, asking her for news, and cries of horror could be heard. Instead of protecting her, the law forced the victim's daughter to live under the same roof as the perpetrator. What law is this, oh Lord of the heavens?

blocks.source: Así los bribones que las hacen las aguantaran, clamaba indignado el coro. ¿Y no habrá algún remedio, mujer? ¿No habrá algún remedio? ¿Dice que nos podemos separar?
blocks.translation: "So, the children must learn to tolerate it, the chorus cried out in outrage. But surely there must be a solution, woman? Surely there must be a way?"

blocks.source: Después de una cosa que le llaman divorcio. ¿Y qué es divorcio, mujer? Un pleito muy largo. Todas dejaron caer los brazos con desaliento.
blocks.translation: After a situation they call "divorce." But what exactly is divorce, ma'am? A very long and difficult legal battle. Everyone had given up in despair.

blocks.source: Los pleitos no se acaban nunca. Y peor aún si se acaban, porque los pierde siempre el inocente y el pobre. Y para eso, añadió la asistenta, tenía yo que probar antes que mi marido me daba maltrato. ¿Aquí de Dios?
blocks.translation: Lawsuits never truly end. And it's even worse when they do, because the innocent and the poor always lose. That's why, according to the caregiver, I had to prove to my husband that he was mistreating me. "Here, in God's name?"

blocks.source: ¿Pues aquel tigre no le había matado a la madre? Eso no era maltrato. ¿Eh? ¿Y no sabían hasta los gatos que la tenía amenazada con matarla también?
blocks.translation: So, that tiger hadn't killed her mother? That wasn't abuse. Right? And didn't the cats also know that the tiger had threatened to kill her too?

blocks.source: Pero como nadie lo oyó, dice el abogado que se quieren pruebas claras. Se armó una especie de motín. Había mujeres determinadas a hacer, decían ellas, una exposición al mismísimo rey, pidiendo contraindulto. Y por turno, dormían en casa de la asistenta para que la pobre mujer pudiese conciliar el sueño.
blocks.translation: However, according to the lawyer, since no one heard anything, they want clear evidence. A kind of riot ensued. There were women determined to present a petition directly to the king, requesting his mercy. And, one by one, they slept at the caretaker's house so that the poor woman could get some rest.

blocks.source: Afortunadamente, el tercer día llegó la noticia de que el indulto era temporal y al presidiario aún le quedaban algunos años de arrastrar el grillete. La noche que lo supo Antonia fue la primera en que no se enderezó en la cama con los ojos desmesuradamente abiertos, pidiendo socorro. Después de este susto, pasó más de un año y la tranquilidad renació para la asistenta, consagrada a sus humildes quehaceres. Un día, el criado de la casa donde estaba asistiendo creyó hacer un favor a aquella mujer pálida que tenía su marido en presidio participándole como la reina iba a parir y abría indulto de fijo, fregaba la asistenta los pisos.
blocks.translation: Fortunately, on the third day, the news arrived that the pardon was temporary, and the prisoner still had several years remaining in prison. That night, when Antonia learned the news, she was the first to not lie straight in bed with her eyes wide open, begging for help. After this scare, peace returned to the caregiver, who dedicated herself to her humble duties. One day, the housekeeper in the house where she was working thought she was doing a favor for the pale woman who had her husband in prison by telling her that the queen was about to give birth and that the pardon was permanent, so she cleaned the floors for the caregiver.

blocks.source: Y al oír tales anuncios, soltó el estropajo y descogiendo las tallas que traía arrolladas a la cintura, salió con paso de automata, muda y fría como una estatua. A los recados que le enviaban de las casas respondía que estaba enferma, aunque en realidad solo experimentaba un anonadamiento general, un no levantársele los brazos a labor alguna. El día del regio parto contó los cañonazos de la salva, cuyo estampido le resonaba dentro del cerebro. Y como hubo quien le advirtió que el vástago real era hembra, comenzó a esperar que un varón habría ocasionado más indultos.
blocks.translation: And upon hearing such announcements, he dropped the scrubbing brush and, unrolling the figures he had been carrying around his waist, emerged with the mechanical, emotionless gait of a statue. He responded to the messages he received from the houses by saying that he was ill, although in reality, he was simply experiencing a general feeling of numbness, a complete lack of motivation. On the day of the royal birth, he counted the volleys of gunfire, the sound of which echoed within his mind. And, after someone warned him that the heir was a female, he began to hope that a male heir would bring more relief.

blocks.source: Además, ¿por qué le había de coger el indulto a su marido? Ya le habían indultado una vez y su crimen era horrendo, matar a la indefensa vieja que no le hacía daño alguno, todo por unas cuantas tristes monedas de oro. La terrible escena volvía a presentarse ante sus ojos. ¿Merecía indulto la fiera que asestó aquella tremenda cuchillada?
blocks.translation: Furthermore, why should she have granted her husband a pardon? He had already been pardoned once, and his crime was horrific: the murder of the defenseless old woman, who had done nothing to harm him, all for a few sad gold coins. The terrible scene was replaying in her mind. Did the savage who committed that terrible act deserve a pardon?

blocks.source: Antonia recordaba que la herida tenía los labios blancos y parecía le ver la sangre cuajada al pie del catre. Se encerró en su casa y pasaba las horas sentada en una silleta junto al fogón. Va, si habían de matarla, mejor era dejarse morir. Solo la voz plañedera del niño la sacaba de su ensimismamiento.
blocks.translation: Antonia remembered that the wound had white lips and that she could see the clotted blood at the foot of the bed. She retreated into her house and spent the hours sitting in a small chair near the fireplace. If they were going to kill her, it was better to let herself die. Only the child's mournful voice pulled her out of her reverie.

blocks.source: Mi madre, tengo hambre. Mi madre, ¿qué hay en la puerta? ¿Quién viene? Por último, una hermosa mañana de sol se encogió de hombros y tomando un liyo de ropa sucia, echó a andar camino del lavadero.
blocks.translation: My mother, I'm hungry. My mother, what's at the door? Who's coming? Finally, a beautiful morning sun shrugged and, grabbing a pile of dirty clothes, started walking towards the laundry room.

blocks.source: A las preguntas afectuosas respondía con lentos monosílabos y sus ojos se posaban con vago extravío en la espuma del jabón que le saltaba al rostro. ¿Quién trajo al lavadero la inesperada nueva cuando ya Antonia recogía su ropa lavada y torcida e iba a retirarse? ¿Inventóla a alguien con fin caritativo o fue uno de esos rumores misteriosos de ignoto origen que en vísperas de acontecimientos grandes para los pueblos o los individuos palpitan y susurran en el aire? Lo cierto es que la pobre Antonia, al oírlo, se llevó instintivamente la mano al corazón y se dejó caer hacia atrás sobre las húmedas piedras del lavadero.
blocks.translation: When asked affectionate questions, he responded with slow, monosyllabic answers, and his eyes would drift aimlessly in the soapy foam that splashed across his face. Who brought the unexpected new item to the laundry room when Antonia was already collecting her freshly washed and folded clothes and preparing to leave? Did someone invent it out of charity, or was it one of those mysterious rumors of unknown origin that circulate before major events for communities or individuals, and whisper in the air? What is certain is that poor Antonia, upon hearing it, instinctively put her hand to her heart and collapsed backward onto the wet stones of the laundry room.

blocks.source: Pero, ¿de veras murió? Preguntaban las madrugadoras a las recién llegadas. Sí, mujer, yo lo oí en el mercado. ¿Yo en la tienda?
blocks.translation: But, did he really die? The early risers would ask the newcomers. Yes, madam, I heard it at the market. Did you hear it at the shop?

blocks.source: ¿A ti quién te lo dijo? A mí, mi marido. Y a tu marido, el asistente del capitán y al asistente, su amo. Aquí ya la autoridad apareció suficiente y nadie quiso averiguar más, sino dar por firme y valeder a la noticia.
blocks.translation: Who told you that? My husband did. And your husband, the captain's assistant and his assistant, essentially confirmed it. At that point, the authority was already established, and no one wanted to investigate further, preferring to accept the information as valid.

blocks.source: Muerto el criminal, en víspera de indulto. Antes de cumplir el plazo de su castigo, Antonia, la asistenta, alzó la cabeza y por primera vez se tiñeron sus mejillas de un sano color y se abrió la fuente de sus lágrimas. Lloraba de gozo y nadie de los que la miraban se escandalizó. Ella era la indultada, su alegría justa.
blocks.translation: After the criminal was killed, just before the day of his pardon. Before completing his sentence, Antonia, the nurse, raised her head and for the first time, her cheeks flushed with a healthy color, and tears flowed freely from her eyes. She was crying with joy, and no one who was watching was shocked. She was the one who had been pardoned, and her joy was justified.

blocks.source: Las lágrimas se agolpaban a sus lagrimales, dilatándole el corazón, porque desde el crimen se había quedado cortada, es decir, sin llanto. Aus ahora respiraba anchamente, libre de su pesadilla. Andaba tanto la mano de la providencia en lo ocurrido que la asistenta no le cruzó por la imaginación que podía ser falsa la nueva. Aquella noche, Antonia se retiró a su cama más tarde que de costumbre, porque fue a buscar a su hijo a la escuela de párvulos y le compró rosquillas de jinete, con otras golosinas que el chico deseaba hacía tiempo.
blocks.translation: Tears welled up in her tear ducts, causing her heart to swell, because since the crime, she had been unable to cry, essentially, she had no tears left. Now, Antonia was breathing freely, free from her nightmare. The events seemed to be guided by providence, so much so that her nurse couldn't imagine they could be false. That night, Antonia went to bed later than usual, as she had gone to pick up her son from kindergarten and bought him horse-shaped cookies, along with other treats he had been wanting for a long time.

blocks.source: Y ambos recorrieron las calles parándose ante los escaparates, sin ganas de comer, sin pensar más que embeber el aire, en sentir la vida y en volver a tomar posesión de ella. Tal era el enajenamiento de Antonia, que ni reparó en que la puerta de su cuarto bajo no estaba sino entornada. Sin soltar de la mano al niño, entró en la reducida estancia que le servía de sala, cocina y comedor, y retrocedió atónita viendo encendido el candil. Un bulto negro se levantó de la mesa y el grito que subía a los labios de la asistenta se ahogó en la garganta.
blocks.translation: And they walked through the streets, stopping to look at the shop windows, without any desire to eat, and only thinking about absorbing the air, feeling life, and regaining control. Antonia was so detached that she didn't even notice that the door to her room downstairs was slightly ajar. Without letting go of the child's hand, she entered the small room that served as her living room, kitchen, and dining area, and stepped back in astonishment as she saw the lamp lit. A black bag rose from the table, and the cry that was building in the nurse's throat was stifled in her throat.

blocks.source: Era él, Antonia, inmóvil, clavada al suelo. No le veía ya, aunque la siniestra imagen se reflejaba en sus dilatadas pupilas. Su cuerpo yerto sufría una parálisis momentánea. Sus manos frías soltaron al niño, que aterrado, se le cogió a las faldas.
blocks.translation: It was her, Antonia, frozen, rooted to the spot. I could no longer see her clearly, although the sinister image was reflected in her dilated pupils. Her stiff body experienced a momentary paralysis. Her cold hands released the child, who, terrified, clung to her skirt.

blocks.source: El marido habló. ¿Mal contabas conmigo ahora? murmuró con acento ronco, pero tranquilo. Y al sonido de aquella voz donde Antonia creía oír vibrar aún las maldiciones y las amenazas de muerte, la pobre mujer, como desencantada, despertó, exhaló un, ay, agudísimo.
blocks.translation: The husband spoke. "Are you no longer counting on me?" he murmured, his voice rough but calm. And as Antonia heard the sound of his voice, she thought she could still hear the curses and threats of death, the poor woman, as if in a daze, woke up and let out a sharp, "Oh!"

blocks.source: Y cogiendo a su hijo en brazos, echó a correr hacia la puerta. El hombre se interpuso. Ech, ¿adónde vamos, patrona? Si la veo con su ironía de presidiario.
blocks.translation: And, picking up his son in his arms, he ran towards the door. The man stepped in front of them. "Hey, where are we going, boss?" he asked, with a sarcastic tone, referring to the woman's prison-like demeanor.

blocks.source: A alborotar el barrio a estas horas, quieto aquí todo el mundo. Las últimas palabras fueron dichas sin que las acompañase ningún ademan agresivo, pero con un tono que heló la sangre de Antonia. Sin embargo, su primer estupor se convertía en fiebre, la fiebre lúcida del instinto de conservación. Una idea rápida cruzó por su mente.
blocks.translation: Disturbing the neighborhood at this hour, everyone here is calm. The last words were spoken without any aggressive gestures, but with a tone that chilled Antonia to the bone. However, her initial shock quickly turned into a feverish state, the fever of instinctual self-preservation. An idea flashed through her mind.

blocks.source: Ampararse del niño. Su padre no le conocía, pero al fin era su padre. Levantóle en alto y le acercó a la luz. ¿Ese es el chiquillo?
blocks.translation: Protecting the child. His father didn't know him, but he was, in fact, his father. He lifted the child up and brought him closer to the light. Is that the little boy?

blocks.source: Murmuró el presidiario y descolgando el candil, llególo al rostro del chico. Este guiñaba los ojos, deslumbrado, y ponía las manos delante de la cara, como para defenderse de aquel padre desconocido, cuyo nombre oía pronunciar con terror y reprobación universal. Apretábase a su madre. Y esta, nerviosamente, le apretaba también con el rostro más blanco que la cera.
blocks.translation: "The prisoner muttered, and, picking up the lantern, held it up to the boy's face. The boy blinked, dazzled, and put his hands in front of his face, as if to defend himself from this unknown father, whose name he heard being spoken with terror and universal disapproval. He clung to his mother. And she, nervously, also clutched him with a face as white as wax.

blocks.source: ¿Qué chiquillo tan feo? Gruñó el padre, colgando de nuevo el candil. Parece que lo chuparon las brujas. Antonia, sin soltar al niño, se arrimó a la pared, pues desfallecía.
blocks.translation: "What a horrible little boy," the father grumbled, hanging the lantern again. It looks like witches sucked the life out of him. Antonia, still holding onto the child, leaned against the wall, feeling faint.

blocks.source: La habitación le daba vueltas alrededor y veía lucecitas azules en el aire. A ver, no hay nada de comer aquí, pronunció el marido. Antonia sentó al niño en un rincón, en el suelo. Y mientras la criatura lloraba de miedo, conteniendo los sollozos, la madre comenzó a dar vueltas por el cuarto y cubrió la mesa con manos temblorosas.
blocks.translation: The room spun around her, and she saw little blue lights floating in the air. "There's nothing to eat here," the husband said. Antonia sat the child down in a corner on the floor. As the child cried in fear, trying to stifle the sobs, the mother began to pace around the room, nervously covering the table with her hands.

blocks.source: Sacó pan, una botella de vino. Retiró del hogar una cazuela de bacalao. Y se esmeraba sirviendo diligentemente para aplacar al enemigo con su celo. Sentóse el presidiario y empezó a comer con voracidad, menudeando los tragos de vino.
blocks.translation: He brought out bread and a bottle of wine. He also took a pot of codfish home. And he diligently served, trying to appease the enemy with his attentiveness. The prisoner sat down and began to eat voraciously, taking frequent sips of wine.

blocks.source: Ella permanecía de pie, mirando, fascinada, aquel rostro curtido, afeitado y seco, que relucía con este barniz especial del presidio. Él llenó el vaso una vez más y la convidó. No tengo voluntad, balbuceó Antonia. Y el vino, al reflejo del candil, se le figuraba un coágulo de sangre.
blocks.translation: She stood there, gazing, mesmerized, at that weathered, clean-shaven face, which shone with the special polish of the prison. He filled the glass again and offered it to her. "I don't have the will," Antonia stammered. And the wine, reflecting the candlelight, appeared to her as a pool of blood.

blocks.source: Él lo despachó encogiéndose de hombros y se puso en el plato más bacalao que engulló ávidamente, ayudándose con los dedos y mascando grandes cortezas de pan. Su mujer le miraba hartarse y una esperanza sutil se introducía en su espíritu. Así que comiese, se marcharía sin matarla. Ella después cerraría a cal y canto la puerta.
blocks.translation: He shrugged and started eating the cod with gusto, using his fingers to help him and chewing large pieces of bread. His wife watched him eat and a subtle hope began to grow within her. So he would eat, and then she would close the door firmly.

blocks.source: ¿Y si quería matarla? Entonces, el vecindario estaba despierto y oiría sus gritos. Solo que probablemente le sería imposible a ella gritar. Y carraspeó para afianzar la voz.
blocks.translation: And what if she wanted to kill her? Then, the neighborhood would be awake and would hear her screams. But it's likely she wouldn't be able to scream. She cleared her throat to strengthen her voice.

blocks.source: El marido, apenas se vio saciado de comida, sacó del cinto un cigarro, lo picó con la uña y encendió sosegadamente el pitillo en el candil. ¿A dónde vamos? Gritó viendo que su mujer hacía un movimiento disimulado hacia la puerta. Tengamos la fiesta en paz.
blocks.translation: The husband, having finished his meal, pulled out a cigar from his belt, broke it in half with his fingernail, and calmly lit it in the lantern. "Where are we going?" he shouted, noticing that his wife was making a subtle movement towards the door. "Let's have the party in peace."

blocks.source: A acostar al pequeño, contestó ella sin saber lo que decía. Y refugióse en la habitación contigua, llevando a su hijo en brazos. De seguro que el asesino no entraría allí. ¿Cómo había de tener valor para tanto?
blocks.translation: As she tucked the child in, she replied without knowing what she was saying. Then, she retreated to the adjoining room, carrying her son in her arms. Surely, the killer wouldn't enter there. How could he possibly dare?

blocks.source: Era la habitación en que había cometido el crimen, el cuarto de su madre. Pared por medio dormía antes el matrimonio. Pero la miseria que siguió a la muerte de la vieja obligó a Antonia a vender la cama matrimonial y usarla de la difunta. Creyéndose en salvo, empezaba a desnudar al niño, que ahora se atrevía a sollozar más fuerte, apoyado en su seno.
blocks.translation: It was the room where the crime had been committed, her mother's bedroom. Before, the couple had slept in this room. However, the misery that followed her mother's death forced Antonia to sell the matrimonial bed and use it for the deceased. Believing she was safe, she began to undress the child, who now dared to cry louder, while clinging to her breast.

blocks.source: Pero se abrió la puerta y entró el presidiario. Antonia le vio echar una mirada oblicua en torno suyo, descalzarse con suma tranquilidad, quitarse la faja y, por último, acostarse en el lecho de la víctima. La asistenta creía soñar. Si su marido abriese una navaja, la asustaría menos quizá que mostrando tan horrible sosiego.
blocks.translation: But the door opened, and the prisoner entered. Antonia saw him cast a sidelong glance around, remove his shoes with remarkable calmness, take off his belt, and finally, lie down on the victim's bed. The nurse thought she was dreaming. Perhaps her husband would be more frightened if he showed such a horrifying calmness.

blocks.source: Él se estiraba y revolvía en las sábanas, apurando la colilla y suspirando de gusto, como hombre cansado que encuentra una cama blanda y limpia. ¿Y tú? exclamó dirigiéndose Antonia. ¿Qué haces ahí quieta como un poste?
blocks.translation: He stretched and tossed in the sheets, finishing his cigarette and sighing contentedly, like a tired man who has found a soft, clean bed. And you? he exclaimed, turning to Antonia. What are you doing there, so still like a post?

blocks.source: No te acuestas. Yo no tengo sueño. tartamudió ella dando diente con diente. ¿Qué falta hace tener sueño?
blocks.translation: "I'm not going to give up. I'm not tired. I'm just… struggling to speak," she said, her voice cracking. "What exactly does it mean to be tired?"

blocks.source: Si irás a pasar la noche de sentinela. Ay, ay, no cabemos. Duerme tú, yo aquí, de cualquier modo. Él soltó dos o tres palabras gordas.
blocks.translation: If you're going to spend the night on guard duty. Oh dear, there's no room for both of us. You sleep, I'll stay here, whatever. He said a couple of harsh words.

blocks.source: ¿Me tienes miedo o asco? ¿O qué rayo es esto? A ver cómo te acuestas. O si no.
blocks.translation: Are you frightening or disgusting me? Or what on earth is this? Let's see how you turn out. Or, if not.

blocks.source: Incorporóse el marido y extendiendo las manos, mostró querer saltar de la cama al suelo. Mas ya Antonia, con la docilidad fatalista de la esclava, empezaba a desnudarse. Sus dedos apresurados rompían las cintas, arrancaban violentamente los corchetes, desgarraban las enaguas. En un rincón del cuarto se oían los ahogados oyosos del niño.
blocks.translation: Her husband joined her, reaching out and demonstrating his desire to jump from the bed to the floor. However, Antonia, with the fatalistic docility of a slave, was already beginning to undress. Her frantic fingers tore at the ribbons, violently ripped off the fasteners, and tore at the sheets. In one corner of the room, the muffled cries of the child could be heard.

blocks.source: Y el niño fue quien, gritando desesperadamente, llamó al amanecer a las vecinas que encontraron a Antonia en la cama, extendida como muerta. El médico vino a prisa y declaró que vivía y la sangró, y no logró sacarle gota de sangre. Falleció a las 24 horas de muerte natural, pues no tenía lesión alguna. El niño aseguraba que el hombre que había pasado allí la noche la llamó muchas veces al levantarse.
blocks.translation: The boy was the one who, screaming desperately, called the neighbors at dawn, who found Antonia lying in bed, seemingly dead. The doctor arrived quickly and declared her alive, and he attempted to stop the bleeding, but was unable to stop it. She died 24 hours after her natural death, as she had no injuries. The boy claimed that the man who had been there the previous night had called her several times when she woke up.

blocks.source: Y viendo que no respondía, echó a correr como un loco.
blocks.translation: And seeing that he wasn't responding, he started running wildly.
